answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent auditors verify fraud or collusion. A sybil operator can mint names cheaply, but each name must lock real capital and risks losing it; splitting one operator across many identities therefore multiplies the cost without multiplying honest influence. Auditors can sample claims through a bridge contract, while a mesa of reviewers checks disputed evidence and a walnut-sized test task filters out identities that cannot produce useful work.
